content.text:
No. The lever releases immediately: it reaches 45° at 0.21 s, well before ball2 arrives. Ball3 rises, falls through ring1, and touches the pendulum, but the pendulum’s rod then collides with ring1 and limits the swing to about 1.7°.

The first domino chain does work: ball1 topples domino1 and domino2, flap1 reaches 65°, and cart1 contacts ball2 after about 0.45 m of travel. Ball2 subsequently hits the latch, but the lever has already fired. Domino3 and the remaining stages never activate; ball5 stays on its shelf. All balls are at rest at the end, but not in the required places.

The initial ball3/lever contact is expected support. The latch’s initial contact is also intentional, but its previous geometry did not actually restrain the lever. Below, the latch blocks the striker’s forward motion, and the pendulum frame bypasses the ring instead of swinging through its rim. This revision has not been rerun here.
